# Bundle Evolution Report

Produces two artifacts for a given set of bundle IDs, built from the dated
`hub-analytics-*-by-bundle.csv` and `hub-analytics-*-detailed.csv` snapshots
in `lib/analytics-output/` (generated by `lib/bin/hub-release-analyzer.js`):

1. **A dependency-free SVG evolution graph** — one row per bundle, cumulative
   downloads plotted across every analytics snapshot, with every published
   version marked on its timeline and an explicit ★ "first release" start
   marker (see [Design notes](#design-notes) for why the start marker matters).
2. **A markdown numbers summary** — overview table plus, per bundle, a
   downloads-by-snapshot table and a versions table (release date, downloads
   at latest snapshot, asset size).

## When to Use

- "Make an evolution graph for bundles X, Y, Z"
- "Chart download growth for these bundles across all analytics snapshots"
- "Extract all the numbers for bundle X into a summary report"
- Any request to visualize or tabulate bundle adoption/version history from
  `lib/analytics-output`

## Procedure

1. **Resolve bundle IDs.** Take the exact bundle IDs from the request. If the
   user gives display names or repo paths instead of bundle IDs, cross-check
   against a `hub-analytics-*-by-bundle.csv` or `-detailed.csv` file to find
   the correct `Bundle ID` values. De-duplicate repeated IDs before proceeding.
2. **Check `lib/analytics-output/` exists** and contains at least one
   `hub-analytics-*-by-bundle.csv` and one `hub-analytics-*-detailed.csv`. If
   analytics look stale, note that to the user (this skill does not run
   `hub-release-analyzer.js` itself).
3. **Generate the graph:**
   ```bash
   python3 .github/skills/bundle-evolution-report/scripts/generate_graph.py \
     --bundle <id-1> --bundle <id-2> --bundle <id-3> \
     --analytics-dir lib/analytics-output \
     --output lib/analytics-output/<descriptive-name>-evolution.svg \
     --title "<Collection/source name>: bundle evolution"
   ```
   Optionally pass `--label <id>:"Display Name"` (repeatable) for friendlier
   row labels than raw bundle IDs.
4. **Generate the summary:**
   ```bash
   python3 .github/skills/bundle-evolution-report/scripts/generate_summary.py \
     --bundle <id-1> --bundle <id-2> --bundle <id-3> \
     --analytics-dir lib/analytics-output \
     --output lib/analytics-output/<descriptive-name>-evolution-summary.md
   ```
5. **Validate the SVG** is well-formed before reporting success:
   ```bash
   python3 -c 'import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET; ET.parse("<output>.svg")'
   ```
   If a browser tool is available, open the SVG and take a screenshot to
   visually confirm rows aren't clipped and version labels aren't overlapping
   (dense release dates on the same bundle can collide — the script already
   staggers labels across 3 lanes, but very dense timelines may still need a
   wider `row_height` tweak in the script).
6. Both scripts raise a clear error (`Missing analytics for: ...`) if a
   requested bundle has no snapshot or release data — surface that to the
   user rather than silently omitting the bundle.
7. Report the output file paths, bundle/version counts, and any data caveats
   (e.g. stale snapshots, bundles present in only one snapshot).

## Design Notes

- **Rows are ordered chronologically by first release date** (oldest on top)
  so the visual order matches the timeline, not an arbitrary input order.
- **Every bundle line is anchored with a synthetic (first-release-date, 0)
  point** rather than starting the line at whatever value its first snapshot
  happened to capture. Without this anchor, bundles that launched between
  snapshots (or have only one snapshot of data) show a floating line start
  with no clear "where did this begin" cue — this was explicit user feedback
  on an earlier version of this graph. The ★ marker + "Launched <date>" label
  make the start unambiguous.
- **Detailed CSVs are cumulative snapshots** — the same release tag appears
  in every snapshot after it was first published, with updated download
  counts. Release dates are deduplicated by keeping the earliest-seen date
  per `(bundle, tag)`; per-version download counts in the summary come from
  the *latest* detailed snapshot only.
- **No third-party dependencies** (no matplotlib) — the graph is generated as
  raw SVG so it works in any environment without package installs.
